title: Leon Wright's showmanship, the dress act and Flip Wilson
summary: Wright steals saxophone battles with Bill Evans and does a dress comedy act with Geesil Minerve that he says Flip Wilson copied.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: I heard you had a very colorful fellow, you did tell the most interesting story about Leon Wright taking the picture. Leon Wright was a fine showman and Bill Evans, they were my two tenor men, Bill Evans and Leon Wright and he would put on such a show, you'd have a battle of the saxes sometimes and poor Leon, compared with what Bill Evans played, was plain nothing, but he would steal the show from him everytime, and we would say Mr. Public
and Leon would do something (inaudible). As I said, I went for the jazz but I was going to put on something that I think would help bring the people in.
You would have a battle of the tenors between Leon and Bill Evans, Yusef Lateef and Leon would steal the show and he was nothing compared to him.

But Bill--Yusef, was very clever too and when he learned it, (inaudible). Yusef was a great, big guy and he would be blowing and blowing and Leon would spread his legs out wide and Leon would get off when he started blowing and just go through his legs and when he would do that the house would go loud. He was quite a showman.

Then we brought up another act, a young man, while we're talking about sax too, we've been talking about those great soloists, but a very fine first alto man was Harold Minerve who now is with the Duke Ellington Band and has been for some years even before Duke

passed. He had a little act that he and Leon used to do together. Leon would put on a dress and they used to do this--remember when Smoke That Cigarette--some country and western band had that--but anyway we had a novelty deal on that and Leon and Harold--Geesil--would put on this act, Leon would have on a dress and so one time I asked him, how did you think of that. He said I used to do this for years and he said-- what's this big comedian--
He said he got that idea from me. He said before I even was in your band I did. He was originally from the east somewhere and he said Flip got that from him.

Look at the picture of him, long before Flip Wilson became famous, it is unbelievable, but it's just like he's doing-- Leon looks like he's doing that Geraldine routine and that came long before Flip Wilson
became famous, so it is possible that he's telling the truth.
